items.title: KREA 2 EDITING IS ABSOLUTELY INSANE!
items.summary:
KREA 2 just received an amazing new update that allows it to transform from a normal image generation model into a powerful image editing model, capable of modifying existing images, preserving identities, swapping heads, changing clothes and much more while still running everything locally!

But I went even further and created my own special LoRA, custom workflow and custom nodes that now allow KREA 2 to properly inpaint and outpaint images while preserving the original aspect ratio, native resolution and overall image quality.

In this video, I will show you how the new KREA 2 editing system works, demonstrate the different editing modes, compare the results and show you how to install everything and get the absolute best results possible from KREA 2!

What do YOU think of the new KREA 2 editing update? Let me know in the comments below!👇

items.title: She Told TikTok No. Three Times.
items.summary: In episode 1013 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Dr. Cathy O'Neil, NY Times Bestselling Author about her algorithmic auditing firm ORCA and her nonprofit Ocean. She explains how these organizations provide crucial statistical evidence for lawsuits against tech companies, proving systemic harm where individual cases are difficult. Dr. O'Neil highlights recent laws in Illinois and Connecticut requiring AI audits and discusses working with lawyers like Meetali Jain on cases against AI chatbots and social media platforms.

Why AI Agents Fail at Reasoning
items.summary:
AI agents can look confident even when their reasoning breaks down.

In this Short, Micheal Lanham, author of AI Agents in Action, Second Edition, explains the most common reasoning failures builders run into, from bad assumptions and brittle plans to tool misuse, hallucinated context, and getting stuck in loops. He also shares how to design around those failures with better evaluation, guardrails, feedback, and human oversight.

Learn more about the book: https://hubs.la/Q04p-7WX0

items.title: Sonar's Approach: Catch AI Slop, Eliminate Technical Debt, Build Resilient Dev Teams
items.summary:
Most engineering teams are racing to ship AI-generated code. Almost none of them know how much of it is quietly broken.

In this episode of Simulated Reality, our host Shalini Mondal sits down with Tariq Shaukat, CEO of Sonar and former President of Bumble and Google Cloud, to discuss why AI agents are generating code 8-15x faster than teams can verify it, how cognitive surrender is eroding engineering judgement across the developer workforce in India and abroad, and why Sonar's guide-verify-solve loop is the structural fix that helps teams scale AI adoption without giving back the productivity gains they hoped to achieve.

items.title: We’re getting closer to “Jarvis” everyday!
items.summary:
Here's how to turn AI into your own personal Jarvis 🤖

By using the voice features on ChatGPT and Claude, you can now build, edit, and iterate on interactive 3D designs in real-time—completely hands-free.

I used voice commands to generate a 3D Iron Man suit, scale the helmet, change the colors, and even add solar panels on the fly.

These voice features are currently free to use on both platforms (available on web and mobile), though paid plans will give you higher usage limits and access to smarter reasoning features.

What would you ask your own personal Jarvis to build first? Let me know in the comments!

And follow for more cool AI and tech tutorials ✅

items.title: Inside the Trading Firm Powering $7 Trillion in Volume | Find Your Edge at Axi
items.summary:
$7 trillion in annual trading volume. Clients in 100+ countries. 10+ offices across four continents.

This is the story of how @AxiOfficialChannel became one of the world's leading, multi-regulated brokers, and where it's headed next.

We went inside to find out what actually powers a business like this. The numbers are staggering. A 200-person team just a few years ago, now over 500. Revenue from $130M to more than double that. A new office in India as the latest foundation in a story still being written. The ambition? To become a top three broker in the world.

But here's what the numbers don't tell you:
Axi executes a trade in under 100 milliseconds, faster than the blink of an eye. It moves over $1 billion in payments a year. It's Manchester City's Official Online Trading Partner. And still, ask anyone inside, and they'll tell you the real edge isn't the speed or the scale. It's the people- the ones who show up with curiosity, grit, and expertise. The ones who live five values every day: Selflessness, Trust, Ambition, Accountability, and Respect. The ones building, in their own words, not just an address but a legacy.

This is a company that keeps building at scale, the best of both worlds. And it's looking for people ready to build with it.

Find your Edge. Join Axi.

items.title: Early Access: Architecting for Autonomy
items.summary:
Architecting for Autonomy teaches you how to update, adapt, and rebuild existing systems so that autonomous AI agents can operate safely and responsibly at scale.

In this session, we’ll ask Anjali & Philip these questions:
1. Why are enterprises struggling to move from AI pilots to real autonomous systems?
2. What’s the difference between automation, copilots, and true autonomy?
3. Where do traditional enterprise architecture models fall short with agentic AI?
4. What is the biggest mistake teams make when introducing autonomous agents?
5. How should architects decide what an AI agent should and shouldn’t be allowed to do?
6. How can enterprises avoid creating uncontrolled “shadow agents”?
7. What does good governance look like when agents can make decisions?
8. How do you design human oversight without slowing everything down?
9. What new security risks appear when agents act on behalf of users or systems?
10. How should companies manage agent identity, permissions, and trust?
11. What does Zero Trust mean in an agentic AI architecture?
12. How can teams make autonomous systems observable and auditable?
13. When does an autonomous system need a kill switch?
14. How should enterprises test agentic systems before putting them into production?
15. What skills do architects need now to design safe, scalable AI autonomy?

This is a live, interactive session, bring your questions for Philip & Anjali.
 
We will also giveaway Ebooks to 2 lucky winners during the session. Comment #AI to enter the raffle!
